Package dev.px.core.hud

Class HudService

java.lang.Object
dev.px.core.hud.HudService
All Implemented Interfaces:
ConfigSection, Named, Service
public final class HudService extends Object implements Service, ConfigSection
Owns the HUD: which elements exist, where each one sits, and drawing them.

The layout engine is entirely here, which is what keeps HudElement down to two mandatory methods. Each frame it asks every element its natural size, applies the element's scale, resolves the anchor formula, clamps the result to the screen, and draws in z-order. None of that is visible to an element.

An element that throws is logged once and skipped for that frame rather than being allowed to kill the overlay: one broken HUD element must not take the rest of the HUD with it.

  • Field Details

    • MIN_VISIBLE

      public static final float MIN_VISIBLE
      How much of an element must remain on screen.

      Elements may hang off an edge deliberately, but never entirely: an element with nothing on screen cannot be found or grabbed in the editor.

      public List<Placement> resolve(boolean includeHidden)
      Resolves every element's on-screen geometry for this frame.

      Returns:
      placements in ascending z-order; equal z keeps registration order

    • place

      public Bounds place(HudLayout layout, Size natural, float screenWidth, float screenHeight)
      Applies the anchor formula, the scale factor and screen clamping.

      Clamping is applied to the resolved position only and is never written back to the layout. Temporarily shrinking the window must not permanently move a user's HUD.

    • hitTest

      public Placement hitTest(List<Placement> placements, float x, float y)
      Returns:
      the topmost placement whose Shape contains the point, or null. Iterated in reverse z-order, so what looks on top wins.

    • renderFrame

      public void renderFrame()
      Draws the HUD, then the editor overlay if it is open.

      Subscribed to Render2DEvent, which is the normal path. An adapter whose editor screen suppresses that event can call this directly instead, but must not do both in the same frame.

    • setAnchor

      public void setAnchor(String id, Anchor anchor)
      Changes an element's anchor without moving it on screen.

      Recomputes the offset so the element stays exactly where it is and only its resize and resolution-change behaviour changes, which is what a user picking a different anchor actually wants.

    • moveTo

      public void moveTo(Placement placement, float x, float y)
